title: AI Adoption Across the Life Sciences Value Chain
summary: Enterprise-wide AI adoption patterns across life sciences from R&D through commercial, including risk management applications and organizational readiness factors. Based on 2021-2022 industry research.

findings.pandemic_acceleration: COVID-19 increased AI focus across the full organization — from R&D (target identification, trial optimization) to manufacturing (yield prediction), supply chain (demand forecasting), and commercial (HCP engagement optimization).
findings.enterprise_ai_approach: Most mature organizations adopt enterprise-wide AI strategies rather than point solutions. This requires centralized data platforms, shared ML infrastructure, cross-functional governance, and a portfolio approach to use case prioritization.
findings.ai_in_risk_management: Emerging applications include: pharmacovigilance signal detection using NLP on unstructured reports, manufacturing quality prediction from process data, supply chain disruption forecasting, and compliance monitoring across promotional activities.
findings.adoption_barriers: Key barriers: data silos across functions, talent scarcity in domain-specific AI/ML, regulatory uncertainty about AI in GxP contexts, organizational resistance to AI-augmented decision-making, and difficulty measuring ROI for enterprise AI investments.
findings.maturity_spectrum: Organizations range from experimenters (isolated proofs of concept) to transformers (AI embedded in core workflows). Most life sciences firms are in the scaling phase — they have successful pilots but struggle to operationalize across the enterprise.

source: Industry research on scaling AI across the life sciences value chain with enterprise-wide and risk management perspectives
